## Left open by the earlier read (RD-153)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule B01 (Blocker). Problem: The flow sends every pre-1973 child of a Filipino mother into the election branch before checking the father. A child who was already Filipino through a Filipino father does not need election. The main prose parent rule and the supplied brief do not support that restriction.
   > Covered by Article IV Section 1(3), born before January 17, 1973 to a mother who was a Filipino citizen when the child was born?
2. Rule L02 (Major). Problem: The added trap requires following a case citation, an oath inside a candidacy certificate, a statutory renunciation rule and foreign-law effects across several paragraphs. This is much denser than the simple explanation of dual citizenship elsewhere and exceeds the Grade 5 teaching standard.
   > In Cordora v. COMELEC, the Court applied Local Government Code Section $40(d)$ to a dual citizen by birth.
3. Rule L23 (Major). Problem: The citizenship flow checks the historical maternal route before paternal citizenship. A pre-1973 child with two Filipino parents is sent to the election decision; the no-election exit never actually checks paternal citizenship. The diagram must route that case correctly.
   > No: Citizenship not established through this route, check another legal basis;
4. Rule L27 (Major). Problem: The residence rule leaves out that the required continuous residence is in the Philippines. The separate administrative-process paragraph says here but does not supply the location for the judicial-naturalization rule.
   > Commonwealth Act $473$, Section $2$, generally requires age $21$ at the hearing and $10$ continuous years of residence.

### Accuracy concerns

1. The flow treats mother and birth date as enough to require election, even where the father already transmitted Philippine citizenship. It needs to distinguish the historical election group from people already citizens through their fathers.
   > Covered by Article IV Section 1(3), born before January 17, 1973 to a mother who was a Filipino citizen when the child was born?
